name: Cost Per Correct
description: Cost Per Correct is a small benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on cost-effectiveness rather than accuracy alone. Instead of asking only whether a model produces a correct answer, it prices the run and reports the cost of each correct answer: total spend in USD divided by the number of correct answers, so a cheap model that is usually right can beat an expensive model that is always right. Version 1.0.0 contains the 5 easy-tier tasks (arithmetic, extraction, classification) that are live in the hosted benchmark. Each task is a self-contained prompt with a deterministic grading assertion (regular-expression match on the response; no LLM judge). The benchmark was created by Karmendra Pandey and first published as a public benchmark on Kaggle Benchmarks on 11 October 2026 (Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge entry), where the live leaderboard remains: https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/karmendra8386/cost-per-correct In the first hosted run (11 October 2026), Gemini 2.5 Flash passed all 5 tasks (leaderboard score 100.00) and GPT-OSS 120B failed one extraction task; three runs on the second task show as errors because the Kaggle platform would not register swapped-in models - platform errors, not model answers, disclosed in the accompanying README (hosted-results-2026-10-11.csv) and in the entry write-up at the time.
